answer: Delayed Entry Capsule: each new agent identity must sit in a nebula queue for a fixed 72-hour dormancy before it can transact, and its first 50 outbound messages are rate-capped to one per minute. An attacker cannot shorten this; spinning up N identities costs N × 72 hours of wall-clock latency plus throttled early throughput, making a hollow mass of fresh accounts unable to act in concert. A falcon-like fast burst from a dormant cohort is flagged and its members lose their remaining capsule window, forcing full re-wait.
